implemented_components.details: Pydantic models for Order (lifecycle states), Vehicle (heterogeneous trucks, edge progress), RoadNetwork (NetworkX graph, traffic multipliers), and FleetState.
Loads Solomon C101, R101, RC101 instances with coordinates, demands, time windows, and service times.
Google OR-Tools CVRPTW solver with time window constraints, vehicle capacity, drop penalties, and multi-objective evaluations.
Bin-packing algorithms (Best Fit Decreasing) and K-Means spatial order clustering.
Physics-based deterministic fuel consumption model tracking vehicle speed, load factor, and gradient.
HistGradientBoosting regressors for travel time, fuel consumption, and customer demand with synthetic data generators.
Traffic dynamics simulator with rush-hour peaks and event engine for discrete disruptions (breakdown, traffic surges, connectivity loss).
Discrete-time simulation environment advancing trucks along road edges, tracking fuel, distance, and order status transitions.
NetworkX-based wireless mesh network modeling transmission range, multi-hop shortest paths, latency, and packet loss.

partially_implemented_components.details: Bidding logic in on_vehicle_breakdown_decentralized locates the winning truck by scanning peer.outbox instead of reading an explicit bidder_vehicle_id from the bid payload.
evaluate_order_absorption and bid response calculate detour_km but omit bidder_vehicle_id, additional_fuel, and additional_co2.
Provides basic distance, fuel, emissions, and lateness calculators, but lacks centralized authoritative calculations for empty km, dynamic vehicle utilization, recovery time, and mesh statistics.
Runs simulation for Centralized vs Resilient agents, but contains heuristic tampering (cent_failed = metrics + len(urgent_orders)), hardcoded mesh_delivery_success=True, and heuristic latency.

broken_components.issue: Lines 103-109 set winning_v_id = winner.get('order_id') (incorrect key) and loop through self.truck_agents searching peer.outbox, which breaks tie-breaking and can assign orders to incorrect vehicles.
cent_failed artificially increments by len(urgent_orders) rather than letting the simulation determine order failures; mesh delivery is hard-coded True.

missing_components.description: Gymnasium Env wrapping SWARMRoute simulation with normalized observation vector, discrete/compact action space, and transparent reward function.
Stable-Baselines3 PPO policy training on real SWARMRoute environment with reproducible seeds and model checkpointing.
Proactive truck repositioning towards zones with high predicted future demand, with empirical comparison against purely reactive dispatch.
Integration of travel time and fuel ML models into candidate route evaluation and bidding.
Comparative evaluation of Nearest Neighbor, OR-Tools, OR-Tools+Prediction, Rule-based recovery, and PPO under identical test scenarios.

missing_components.description: Visual diagram/plot of the breakdown recovery flow and JSON record.

integration_problems: Prediction models in src/prediction/ are isolated and never called during routing, route re-optimization, or agent bidding.
Mesh transmission metrics (hops, latency, packet success) are tracked inside MeshNetwork but not gathered authoritatively into the simulation environment get_metrics() output.
scientific_correctness_problems: Manual addition to failed orders in experiments.py (cent_failed = ... + len(urgent_orders)) violates empirical simulation integrity.
Bidding winner selection depends on dictionary order rather than strict multi-criteria deterministic evaluation (feasible -> min detour -> min fuel -> min co2 -> vehicle_id tie-break).
Comparison between Centralized and Decentralized controllers needs exact synchronization of initial conditions, orders, dynamic events, and simulation clock.
